scope: Cross-check an open-source peer's reported repeated ACDSDATA group-310 readback loss against the DXF limit and local libdxfrw writer, qualification, and generated test coverage; update existing implementation readiness without asserting a local defect or promoting 3D support.

method.kind: Primary standards, project pull-request discussion, and local source/test audit
method.evidenceRule: A peer contributor's branch-level report is not a release result or a local defect. Source inspection establishes intended code paths only; generated multi-chunk runtime coverage is still required. A carrier transport test does not establish valid SAB, B-rep semantics, or consumer acceptance.

evidence.observed: The official DXF group-code reference defines codes 310-319 as arbitrary binary chunks and limits each hexadecimal value to 254 characters, representing at most 127 bytes.
evidence.planUse: Use a 256-byte generated payload to require three chunks with 127/127/2 bytes and 254/254/4 hex characters.

evidence.observed: An Oct. 1 contributor comment on open PR #1150 says that after an ACDS refactor the DXF reader retained only the last group-310 line of an ACDSDATA record and asks for #1268's chunk-joining fix first. The current PR page shows #1150 open with no deployment or review. The exact merge/release state of #1268 was not established in this review.
doesNotEstablish: a defect in ACadSharp master or any released package
that #1268 has or has not shipped
semantic validity of an ACIS body or native application acceptance
evidence.planUse: Treat as a branch-level regression lead. A future peer run must pin exact source/release and artifact identity.

sources: dwg2dxf/dx_iface.cpp: ACDSDATA projection loop using bytesPerChunk = 127
src/libdxfrw.cpp: hasQualifiedAc1027AcdsRecord repeated group-310 accumulation and group-94 length check
evidence.observed: Local code emits ordered 127-byte group-310 chunks. The AC1027 modeler qualification path iterates repeated group-310 values, decodes/appends them, and checks declared length and entity payload identity. This is a source-level observation, not a runtime result.
evidence.planUse: Do not alter production code absent a failing generated test; first close the explicit multi-chunk coverage gap.

evidence.observed: The existing generated modeler payloads are 18 bytes and thumbnail payloads are below 127 bytes. The test checks payload equality, owner keys, schema, and ASCII/binary import, but no individual record has more than one group-310 chunk and this helper does not replay the multi-record output.
evidence.planUse: Extend this existing fast test owner with a deterministic 256-byte modeler payload, exact chunk assertions, and second-pass replay in ASCII and binary.

fastSlice: Use a leading-signature, 256-byte transport-only modeler payload in the existing ASCII and binary ACDSDATA projection test.
Assert exactly three ordered group-310 chunks of 127/127/2 bytes, declared group-94 length 256, correct ASM_Data schema/property and group-320 source owner key, with no bleed into adjacent records.
Import, replay to a second temporary output, and re-import; compare exact bytes and expected owner remapping.
If cheap, include omitted-middle and reordered-chunk negative controls that refuse without modifying a seeded destination.
Run the strict touched target, focused libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip CTest, and scoped git diff --check only.
